title: RSI: Run boundaries
question: What counts as one skill use, and when is it finished?

origin.title: RSI: Run boundaries
origin.question: What counts as one skill use, and when is it finished?

history.reason: Capture an unresolved choice from the agent proposal before the owner first pass; alignment only.

proposal.readback:
**Question:** What counts as one skill use, and when is it finished?

**Recommended answer:** One requested operation is one use, with linked child skill uses. Preserve its identity across pauses and resumed chats. Record completion, cancellation, interruption and reopening separately.

**Why:** I chose these boundaries without asking. Counting chats or file reads as uses would distort outcomes and recurrence.

**Intended impact:** Determines run counts, attribution, completion triggers and recovery behavior.

proposal.readback:
**Question:** What counts as a skill use, what do we record, and when does a failure enter the RSI loop?

**Recommended answer:** Whenever you, Codex or Claude use a participating Workbench skill to perform an operation, record that use and its outcome. One requested operation is one use, even across resumed chats; separately invoked skills have linked uses. Record the skill version, model tier/provider and whether the work completed, failed or was interrupted. Record reported failures immediately and mark them as needing repair. Repair can start after the current work or at the designated time, as agreed in question 7.

**Why:** Real work supplies the failure cases and evidence of value. Recording successful uses as well as failures gives us the denominator needed to determine whether errors decrease. Prompt capture preserves findings without requiring repairs to interrupt your work.

**Intended impact:** Every participating skill has a traceable use history. A reported failure becomes a durable RSI input immediately, and later results can show whether repairs reduce recurrence during real work.

proposal.readback:
**Question:** What do we record for each skill use, and when and where should repairs happen?

**Recommended answer:** Record each participating skill use, its version, model tier/provider, outcome and reported failures. One requested operation remains one use across resumed chats, with linked uses for other invoked skills. Record failures immediately. Start repairs after the current work finishes. If a failure blocks that work, record it as a critical failure and start the repair in a new chat. Preserve the original session’s continuation so it can resume with the fixed skill once the repair is verified and the repaired version is available to that session.

**Why:** Non-blocking repairs should not interrupt useful work. A blocking skill failure needs a separate repair context while preserving the original task and its continuation.

**Intended impact:** Real work builds the shared failure and use history. Routine repairs follow completed work; critical blockers get a separate repair chat that returns a usable fix to the original session.
proposal.why: Non-blocking repairs should not interrupt useful work. A blocking skill failure needs a separate repair context while preserving the original task and its continuation.
